more.title: 3D model generates most detailed picture yet of what's going on beneath West Antarctica's melting ice
more.summary: Donna dePolo and Shijie Zhong have never set foot on Antarctica. But with the help of satellites measuring ground motions and gravity, a supercomputer in Wyoming and years of seismic data collected at remote Antarctic research stations, the CU Boulder physicists have created a detailed picture of what's been happening beneath the West Antarctic ice as it rapidly melts.

more.title: Universities should follow communities' lead on climate research

more.title: Euclid's H-alpha observations map where stars form in distant galaxies
more.summary: Euclid was launched into space in July 2023 to explore two of astronomy's biggest mysteries: dark matter and dark energy. The space telescope's first major data release covers some 1,900 square degrees of the sky, equivalent to around 14% of the area planned for the six-year mission and around 5% of the total sky. It is an unprecedented collection of visible and near-infrared observations.

more.author: Charlie Wood

more.title: The sun, Earth, Jupiter and white dwarfs: Potential traps for dark matter
more.summary: Dark matter continues to evade direct detection. Its slower-moving particles might leave signals too faint for detectors to register, yet be more easily captured by planets and stars. As they accumulate inside these bodies, they could produce effects that existing instruments would allow us to search for.

more.title: What makes food 'organic?' For many consumers, the answer isn't always on the label
more.summary: "Organic" is a word we encounter every time we visit the supermarket. It's also one that can mean very different things to different people.

more.title: Report finds consistent pandemic learning loss and gaps between grades and test scores across Canada
more.summary: A new national report identifies declines in student performance in every province and territory examined in Canada, with grade inflation obscuring the extent of setbacks during the COVID-19 pandemic.

more.title: Mourning Notcho: What one whale's death teaches us about ecological grief
more.summary: Sighting a humpback whale from a boat can be awe-inspiring. For some BC Ferries passengers, that experience became disturbing when their ferry struck and fatally injured a humpback whale on Oct. 18.

more.title: After dodging death, battery startup Our Next Energy is now going public

more.summary: Our Next Energy is the latest battery startup to go public via SPAC. Does it now have what it needs to survive in the cutthroat battery industry?

more.title: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain
more.summary: New research reveals that biological sex, genetics, and menopause may dramatically influence Alzheimer's risk, treatment responses, and chronic pain conditions such as fibromyalgia. Scientists also uncovered surprising differences in immune activity and gut-brain interactions, opening the door to more personalized treatments for neurological disorders.

more.title: Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock
more.summary: Deep beneath the Pacific Ocean, scientists have discovered tiny hidden ecosystems inside metal-rich rocks that take millions of years to form. Researchers examined 244 nodules and found more than 4,100 animals living in their cracks and cavities, including unique communities unlike those in the surrounding seafloor mud.

more.title: Could your personality be affecting how you feel about social media?
more.summary: Social media offers everyone the same basic promise: post something about yourself and get responses from other people. Whether it's a vacation, a promotion or just a midweek meal, these days many people's lives are shared online.

more.title: 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?
more.author: VicOne
more.summary: This article is brought to you by VicOne . VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others. Based on initial validation, all 28 findings are classified as zero-day vulnerabilities.

more.title: Flat optics roadmap charts path toward smaller imaging and sensing systems
more.summary: For centuries, optical systems have relied on lenses, mirrors and other components that manipulate light through their shape and size. Today, advances in nanotechnology are enabling a different approach. Researchers can now engineer materials at scales smaller than the wavelength of light, creating ultrathin optical components that offer new ways to control how light behaves.
